title: Geometric inverse image preserves constant module sheaves
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism, that is, an adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ on sheaves of sets whose left adjoint preserves finite limits. Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-module, with no finiteness assumption. Write $\underline M_{\mathcal C},\underline M_{\mathcal D}$ for the sheafifications of the constant module presheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the module inverse image $f_R^*$ and canonical identification $f^{-1}\underline R_{\mathcal C}\cong\underline R_{\mathcal D}$ of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. There is a canonical isomorphism $f_R^*\underline M_{\mathcal C}\cong\underline M_{\mathcal D}$ of $\underline R_{\mathcal D}$-module sheaves, natural in all $R$-linear maps $M\to N$. On underlying sheaves of sets it is the comparison obtained by expressing the constant sheaf of the set $M$ as the sheaf coproduct of $M$ copies of the terminal sheaf and applying $f^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf, its universal property; Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi (modules over a fixed ring).

proof.text: For a set $E$, let $P_E$ be the constant presheaf and let $1$ denote the terminal sheaf, whose underlying presheaf is constant singleton. Sectionwise, $P_E$ is the coproduct of $E$ copies of that presheaf. Thus a presheaf map $P_E\to H$ to any sheaf $H$ is exactly a family $(1\to H)_{e\in E}$. By the sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], maps $\underline E\to H$ are the same families. This proves directly that $\underline E=\coprod_{e\in E}1$, with injections $\iota_e$ given by constant sections, including $E=\varnothing$. A set map $a:E\to F$ induces the sheaf map characterized by $\iota_e\mapsto\iota_{a(e)}$.

source.place: Tag 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf; universal property of sheafification, Tag 00WH

proof.text: The hypothesis on $f^{-1}$ identifies $f^{-1}1_{\mathcal C}$ with $1_{\mathcal D}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ and the discrete diagram indexed by the set $E$; this diagram is small in the fixed coefficient universe and its colimit was constructed in Step 1. Hence $f^{-1}\underline E_{\mathcal C}$ is a coproduct of $E$ copies of $1_{\mathcal D}$. Its universal property gives the unique isomorphism $c_E:f^{-1}\underline E_{\mathcal C}\to\underline E_{\mathcal D}$ carrying each $f^{-1}\iota_e$ to $\iota_e$. For $a:E\to F$, the two maps $c_F f^{-1}(\underline a)$ and $\underline a c_E$ agree after every coproduct injection, so they agree. Thus $c$ is natural in all set maps.

source.place: Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact (1); with sites.tex Tag 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact], $\underline{E\times F}$ identifies with $\underline E\times\underline F$ through the two projections, and $\underline{\{*\}}=1$. Since $f^{-1}$ preserves finite limits, naturality of Step 2 with respect to these projections implies $c_{E\times F}=c_E\times c_F$ under these identifications: the two projections of both maps are equal, so the product universal property proves equality. Also $c_{\{*\}}$ is the terminal comparison. By [lem-cbc-module-sheafification-underlying-sets] with $P$ the constant $R$-module presheaf, the underlying set sheaf of $\underline M$ is exactly the set constant sheaf used above, compatibly with its constant sections. The same compatibility for the constant ring follows from [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets].

source.place: Tag 00WJ, lemma-sheafification-exact; Tag 00YR, section-sheaves-algebraic-structures, sheafification/forgetful comparison

proof.text: Use [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] for $\Lambda=R$, so the operations of $f_R^*\underline M$ are obtained by applying $f^{-1}$ to the source operations. Naturality of $c$ for $+:M\times M\to M$, $0:\{*\}\to M$ and $-:M\to M$, together with Step 3, gives $c_M f^{-1}(+)=+\,(c_M\times c_M)$, $c_M f^{-1}(0)=0$ and $c_M f^{-1}(-)=-\,c_M$. For the action $\mu:R\times M\to M$ it gives $c_M f^{-1}(\mu)=\mu\,(c_R\times c_M)$. Here [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] identifies the action on the constant module sheaf with the sheafification of this constant-presheaf action. The ring comparison $c_R$ agrees with the canonical ring identification in the inverse-image node: both carry every constant scalar injection to that scalar, and the coproduct universal property in Step 2 forces equality. Consequently $c_M$ is a morphism of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Its inverse is linear: substituting $x=c_M^{-1}(y)$ in $c_M(ax)=a c_M(x)$ and applying $c_M^{-1}$ gives $c_M^{-1}(ay)=a c_M^{-1}(y)$, and the same argument gives additivity. It therefore gives the asserted module isomorphism.

For an $R$-linear map $h:M\to N$, Step 2 applied to its underlying set map says $c_N f^{-1}(\underline h)=\underline h c_M$. The inverse-image functor in Step 4 acts on maps by the underlying inverse image, so this is precisely the naturality square in module sheaves. Step 2 also proves that the underlying set comparison is the coproduct comparison required by the statement.

source.place: Tag 0H7J and Tag 00YV, naturality on structure-preserving maps

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q122-269842107 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all five steps and every cited statement in full. Sources checked: Stacks sites.tex 0H7J example-constant-sheaf (l.2099), 00YV (l.10473), 00WJ (l.2134), and categories.tex 0038 lemma-adjoint-exact (1) (l.3472). The proof is correct. Step 1: the constant sheaf of E is the coproduct of E copies of the terminal sheaf, by the sheafification universal property; this holds for E empty and with empty covers. Step 2: left-adjoint colimit preservation applies, with a small discrete index, the colimit from Step 1 and the adjunction from the hypothesis; left exactness sends 1 to 1. Step 3: product compatibility via sheafification-sets-exact, plus the underlying-set leaves for module and ring sheafification. Step 4: I checked it against how lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image builds the action, L(a_M)p^{-1}(c^{-1}x1). The step shows c_R equals the canonical c on scalar summands, and naturality for mu gives linearity. The interface leaf identifies the constant module action with the set sheafification of mu. The inverse is linear. Step 5 is naturality. No new nodes. The coefficient category is modules over the constant ring sheaf, which matches the parent's use for nu_X and nu_{V_i}; no target node or base-change morphism is involved. Small cases checked: M=0, E empty, E a singleton, f=id, zero ring. No cycle, and proof_deps equals the union of uses. Duplicate search over DAG constant/inverse-image nodes (sbc-geometric-point-module-constant, pbc-constant-ring-inverse-image-comparison, pbc-constant-module-section-coefficients, proetale-constant-ring-map and others) found none, and Mathlib has no matching leaf. Accepted tool_uses: lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image (unit sk-prop-sf-comparison, a generic inverse-image construction) and lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface (a Mathlib leaf).
